title: $λ$-geodesic convexity of the squared sliced-Wasserstein distance
summary: The squared Wasserstein distance with respect to a fixed target measure is not a convex function along Wasserstein geodesics over $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $d\geq 2$. Still, in dimension $d=1$, this function is $2$-geodesically convex. We prove that the square of the sliced-Wasserstein distance (which is a distance constructed averaging one-dimensional Wasserstein distances) is $λ$-geodesically convex (possibly with $λ\leq 0$) on sets of measures satisfying upper bounds on their density, when the target measure satisfies some given geometric conditions.
